Assignment 2 — Cross-Grower EDA Report

Field boundaries · CDL cropland data · Weather patterns · IL · IA · NE

1. Dataset Scope

Three growers were created using the My Farm Advisor data pipeline, each with one farm and ten fields sampled from OpenStreetMap via the Overpass API. The pipeline automatically selected the top corn-producing county in each state by querying the 2025 CDL (Cropland Data Layer) raster.

1a. Grower Locations

Three growers with ten fields each:
Illinois (il-grower) — Iroquois County, IL (FIPS 17075). East-central IL, typical row-crop region.
Iowa (ia-grower) — Kossuth County, IA (FIPS 19109). North-central IA, intensive corn/soy production.
Nebraska (ne-grower) — Perkins County, NE (FIPS 31135). Southwest NE along the Platte River valley, extensive center-pivot irrigation.

2. Data Layers Used

All data was generated by the full default pipeline and stored under the runtime root. No soil data was loaded or analyzed.

Field boundaries — field_boundaries.geojson (EPSG:4326) with area_acres, county_name, field_id.
CDL / Cropland Data Layer — NASS USDA CDL rasters (30 m, 2021–2025), extracted per field as crop composition tables and rotation summaries.
Weather — NASA POWER daily time series (2021–2025) at field centroids: T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, PRECTOTCORR, and derived GDD (base 10°C).
Geoadmin — US state boundaries from Census Tiger Line (2025) for the overview map base.

3. Comparison Levels

The analysis covers four levels of comparison, each supported by specific data.

Within a field — Weather time series (daily, 2021–2025) captures year-to-year and seasonal variability for each individual field.
Field-year — CDL composition is available per field per year, showing crop choice changes over the 5-year window.
Across fields within a grower — Field boundary area, crop diversity, and rotation patterns are compared among the 10 fields within each state.
Across growers — All plots directly compare IL vs IA vs NE using consistent metrics and identical pipeline processing.

4a. Field Boundaries — Statistical Visualizations

Two statistical views of field area by state: a density histogram showing the full distribution shape and a summary bar chart with mean ± standard deviation.

4b. Field Boundaries — Comparison / Correlation

Side-by-side box plot for direct distribution comparison across the three states.

5a. CDL / Cropland — Statistical Visualizations

Two views of crop history: a stacked bar showing the dominant crop percentages per grower and a box plot of per-field crop diversity.

5b. CDL / Cropland — Comparison / Correlation

Grouped bar chart comparing mean corn years vs soybean years per field across states.

6a. Weather — Statistical Visualizations

Two climate summaries: the mean monthly temperature cycle and total annual precipitation, both averaged across fields within each state.

6b. Weather — Comparison / Correlation

Cumulative growing degree days (GDD, base 10°C) across the calendar year, averaged over all fields and years per state.

7. Geospatial Map

A base map of US states with field centroid markers and field ID labels.

8. Key Findings

Field size — Nebraska fields are substantially larger (mean ~400+ ac) than Iowa (~130 ac) and Illinois (~90 ac), driven by center-pivot irrigation layouts.
Crop rotation — All three states are corn-soybean dominant. Illinois shows the most balanced rotation; Nebraska has the highest corn frequency.
Precipitation gradient — IL/IA receive ~2× the annual precipitation of NE, confirming the reliance on irrigation in Nebraska.
Growing season — NE has the highest GDD accumulation, supporting longer-season corn hybrids.
Crop diversity — Most fields grow 2–3 crops; diversity is similar across states despite different field sizes and climates.

9. Limitations & Assumptions

Sample size — 10 fields per state is a small sample. Individual field boundaries were selected from OSM and may not represent the full county or state distribution.
Boundary source — OSM/Overpass field boundaries are crowd-sourced; accuracy varies and some fields may include or exclude non-agricultural areas.
CDL resolution — 30 m pixels may misclassify small features or field edges. The 5-year CDL window (2021–2025) is the available range, not a full historical record.
Weather data — NASA POWER provides grid-cell estimates (~0.5°) that smooth local variability. Actual on-farm weather may differ, especially for convective precipitation events.
GDD calculation — GDD uses the standard (Tmax+Tmin)/2 – 10°C formula with no upper cutoff. Daily values assume uniform temperature distribution.
Time range — All analyses cover 2021–2025. Patterns may differ over a longer climate window.

10. Soil Analysis

Soil analysis was not required and was not performed.

The Assignment 2 EDA scope explicitly excluded soil data. All visualizations and comparisons are based on field boundaries, CDL/cropland data, and weather time series. The pipeline's SSURGO soil outputs exist for each field but were not loaded, queried, or plotted in this analysis.
